Architecture · Research recordArchitecture document ↗

From input to an observed path.

Mindscape turns an input into explicit state, a policy proposal, an executed action, a recorded transition, and an independently verified result. Its architecture makes that path inspectable while keeping direct observations separate from interpretations of why an output occurred.

The project has two backends with different mechanisms. Numeric tasks use a small trained MLP; coding tasks use pinned Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B weights and adapters. Their controllers, representations, and tools must be understood separately.

Recorded diagnostics

Two CPU float32 diagnostics reuse one historical coding task. They add no benchmark accuracy cases. This explorer shows selected actual recorded events from the source page; the complete source evidence remains checksum-bound in the research archive.

Methods
Two backends. Different mechanisms.
The numeric backend uses a small trained MLP over operands, explicit state, and previous-action features. Its deterministic environment performs arithmetic, and legal-action masking can supply the next valid action. This makes numeric execution an environment-policy-controller system; success cannot automatically be attributed to learned neural computation.
The coding backend uses pinned Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B weights and adapters, structured repository state, bounded memory, typed tools, static planner hypotheses, and independent verification. Implemented components differ by condition.

Memory and hypothetical proposals
Working memory resets per episode. Bounded experience memory is built from executed training examples. Dreaming is a bounded hypothetical proposal mechanism, not executed experience or autonomous discovery. Planner predictions remain hypotheses until an environment action produces an actual result.
Coding architecture ↗Numeric architecture ↗
Observation boundaries
A trace is evidence. It does not, by itself, explain why a model produced an output. The recorded diagnostics capture selected paths through a specific implementation.
  • Exact generate arguments, direct forward token IDs, logits, shapes, component invocations, and environment transitions were captured for the selected live diagnostics.
  • Probabilities are derived, uncalibrated softmax summaries. Activation and probability visualizations do not establish causal explanations.
  • Historical coding prompts and logits were not retained and cannot be reconstructed as direct observations.
  • Hidden activations and live coverage of every historical adapter remain unmeasured.
  • Numeric hidden summaries are explicitly reconstructed from observed features and weights.
  • Causal claims are limited to declared controlled software interventions.
Read computation tracing and its limits ↗
Ablations and interventions
To test a component, keep the control fixed. The numeric factorial study manipulated legal-action masking, state-feature readout, and previous-action readout at fixed trained weights. Readout removal does not remove the entire memory module.
The subsequent zero-weight control tested whether trained neural information was necessary with the controller enabled. Verification, environments, and action budgets remained fixed. All unsuccessful outcomes were retained.
Observation and intervention answer different questions.
A diagnostic records what occurred. A controlled intervention tests how a declared change affects outcomes under fixed conditions. Neither supports claims beyond its measured scope.
Further work remains: independent cross-domain and training-pipeline replication, broader adapter coverage, selected hidden activations, matched historical-model comparisons with approved access, and more precise confirmatory measurement.
